_answer_key: Answer_Keys/Final Answer Key for recuitment of Jr. Grade of MES (AE SDO) under PHE Department..pdf (sha256:c2a6cf3b9a9850d3), General Studies page, Final Answer Key notified 21 March 2024 under No. MES/A/2023-MPSC for the examination held 23-25 January 2024
_files_live_in: mpsc-question-bank repo - a DIFFERENT repo, hence this transcription
_filename_typo: The paper is filed as 'General Stadies', not 'General Studies'. That typo hid it from every subject-word search in the previous two sessions' surveys - search by exam name too.
_paper_extraction: THE PAPER IS A PURE SCAN: an 8-character text layer, so there is no machine text to trust and OCR is unavoidable. Rendered at 400 dpi and OCR'd twice with different page segmentation: --psm 4 DETACHED the question numbers into a gutter column on page 2, which would have mis-aligned every number against its stem - the silent-misalignment failure this project keeps warning about - so --psm 6, which keeps them attached, is the scaffold and psm4 only a second read. Then all 8 pages were READ BY EYE at 170 dpi and the scaffold corrected: every correction in the script's FIX table is what the page actually says, not a guess. The one that mattered most is Q17, which OCR gave as 'If 7°=343, then 3/343' and the page prints as 'If 7³=343, then ∛343' - unanswerable as OCR'd. Verified: 100 sequential questions, each with exactly options A-D, none empty, none still carrying OCR litter, and every key letter is one of its question's options.
_key_extraction: NOT OCR'd. The key PDF has a real 29,739-char text layer, so its General Studies page was parsed the same way as July-2023's: every '<n> (<A-D>)' pair on the page, aborting if any question number yields two different letters. 100/100 entries. So the answers are machine-read from clean text even though the questions had to be eye-verified from a scan.
_key_quality: All 100 answers were checked independently, including working every quantitative item by hand (Q13 cubes, Q14, Q17, Q48 page digits, Q49 pass marks, Q55 perimeters, Q56-62, Q79, Q81 direction trace, Q82 house puzzle, Q83, Q84 pair-swap code, Q85 seating, Q86 work rates, Q87 percentage error). Every one agrees with the key. Two are contested and say so on the card: Q15 (the analogy's keyed answer looks wrong) and Q35 (the question is internally inconsistent as printed - see the tags file).
